correctness.rationale: Recovery completeness plus a direct tree-dual argument characterizes target nonrecovery as membership in an unmarked simple tree component in the large-\(x\) limit. Independent Poisson vertex and edge processes give the displayed exact finite-\(k\) survival probability. Its fixed-size component terms converge to the rooted-tree series, component-size tails are controlled by the no-mark factor, and \(U_k(r)\le e^{-ar}\) gives dominated convergence in time. The tree function solves \(u=e^{-ar-2(1-a)r(1-u)}\), and a monotone change of variables yields exactly the LT degree-\(2\) integral. The standard-library verifier independently checks the finite-\(k\) integrated formula and the numerical KKT root.

value.rationale: The finding resolves an explicit 2026 conjecture linking the strongest known ideal-decoding degree-\(2\) construction to the LT peeling optimum. It gives a complete one-parameter asymptotic formula, identifies the unique optimal ratio, and explains structurally why ideal cycle recovery has no first-order advantage in this positive-mark regime. This closes a motivated gap rather than merely recomputing a numerical optimum.
